data.title: Blue Ant Media expands share buyback program
data.description:
• Blue Ant Media (BAMI:CA)  said it will increase the size of its normal course issuer bid to 1.81M subordinate voting shares from 1.09M, effective Aug. 25.
  • The company will also raise its daily repurchase limit to 7,582 shares from 1,000. Blue Ant had repurchased 108,300 shares under the program as of July 31.

data.title: Taming bond yields: What else can Bessent pull out of the Treasury toolkit?
data.description:
It's been quite a few days for the U.S. bond market, with investors still sizing up the latest fallout and where things may go from here. Under the direction of Secretary Scott Bessent, the U.S. Treasury on Wednesday announced that it would double its buybacks to serve as a backstop for longer-maturity government bonds (a.k.a. preventing the 30-year Treasury yield from continuing its upward trajectory). While the maneuver initially knocked the 30-year yield (US30Y) down 10 basis points to 5.19%, the relief was short-lived as yields quickly resumed their climb back to 5.26% during trading on Thursday.

What's at play? There's been a debate surrounding why yields are rising, as well as what to do about it—if anything. Note that yields have been on the march higher for years, but more recently, concerns over government debt, the amount of corporate issuance, poor liquidity, or plain old vigilantism might be to blame. It's a reason for concern. Higher bond yields mean that the Treasury is locking in higher borrowing costs, which can translate into even larger deficits barring some serious economic growth. As a result, the U.S. Treasury is figuring out its options, while some warn that any intervention won't change the fundamentals and to leave market forces alone.

"We have a big toolkit, so we'll see. And part of it is signaling here," Bessent declared, unveiling a twist operation of buying back longer-dated bonds with cash raised from short-term sales. While this is a routine operational mechanism, there are concerns here for the dollar, or should the program be prolonged or increase in size. "Governments trying to control markets is not a particularly attractive story most of the time," noted JPMorgan's James Sullivan. "It's a little bit like paying your mortgage with your credit card. It can work for a while, but eventually the mismatch becomes more obvious."

Outlook: What else can the Treasury do to cap yields and keep bond volatility out of the headlines? Bessent's $4B buyback target is tiny a faction of the the total $32T Treasury market, so the program could be ramped up even further. Bessent is also planning an upcoming press conference to discuss fiscal consolidation, but other immediate ideas may include cutting down the issuance of longer-dated debt or altering bank capital rules to boost demand. In case of an emergency, the U.S. Treasury could coordinate with the Federal Reserve on the yield curve, its balance-sheet runoff, or global central banks on joint interventions to reduce foreign selling pressure on U.S. debt.

data.title: Goldman Sachs expands into India's government share sale market - report
data.description:
Goldman Sachs (GS) is expanding into the Indian government's share sale market, an area that has traditionally been dominated by local finance giants, Bloomberg News reported.

The New York-based Wall Street giant has served as an adviser for five of the 10 major transactions that took place since the latest divestments started in December last year, the report published on Friday noted.

The transactions include the Life Insurance Corp. of India's $3.3B secondary offering through a stock exchange, according to Bloomberg.

GS is said to be behind only Kotak Mahindra Bank in initial and second offerings so far in 2026, having surpassed Axis Bank (AXBKY) and ICICI Bank (IBN).

Citigroup (C) (CITI:CA) and BNP Paribas (BNPQF) (BNPQY) (BNP:CA) have also been a part of the market, the report noted.

The government of India is reportedly targeting raising 800B rupees for the financial year ending March 2027.

India ETFs: (INDA), (IMVP), (FLIN), (INDY), (SMIN), (INDL), (GLIN), (INCO), (NFTY), (EPI), (DGIN), (NDIA), (INDE), (GIND), (INDH)

data.title: AXT in focus as Wedbush weighs in on potential China delays
data.description:
• Amid a report that China is delaying the passage of certain critical materials such as germanium, quartz, and neodymium, it hasn't yet impacted semiconductor materials companies, Wedbush Securities said.
  • “China's role as a key supplier of critical materials and the Chinese government's willingness to moderate or halt supply remain points to watch given key elements (like rare earths or indium) are often core building blocks required for data center necessities (motors, optics, etc.), with past shortages of neodymium for instance having weighed heavily on the HDD industry,” Wedbush Securities analyst Matt Bryson wrote in a note to clients. “Having said this, it has appeared lately that China's reluctance to ship product freely hasn't risen to the level of extremely disruptive for most of our coverage (ex. AXTI), and rather proven to be a potential stumbling block that requires management.”
  • AXT is one of the larger manufacturers of indium phosphide, gallium arsenide, and germanium, all of which have many uses, including in semiconductors.

data.title: Docebo raises buyback price to $25/share, extends offer deadline
data.description:
• Docebo (DCBO) has raised the price of its previously announced $70M share buyback to $25 per share, up from $20.40, and extended the offer deadline to Sept. 8, 2026.
  • The higher price reduces the maximum number of shares the company can repurchase to 2.8M, compared to 3.4M shares previously. All other terms remain unchanged.

data.title: Arbutus to repurchase up to $230M of shares in tender offer
data.description:
• Arbutus Biopharma (ABUS) said it plans to launch a modified Dutch auction tender offer to repurchase up to $230M of its common shares at $5 to $5.75 per share.
  • The offer is expected to begin on or around Aug. 24 and expire around Sept. 29, with the company using cash on hand to fund the repurchases.
  • Stock up 12% in Friday premarket trading.

data.title: Marvell's deal with Google indicates that custom silicon is 'advantageous,' Wedbush says
data.description:
Marvell Technology's (MRVL) announcement this week that it is working with Google (GOOG) (GOOGL) to develop custom AI chips is indicative that custom silicon is “advantageous,” Wedbush Securities said.

“Net, we don't see this outcome as necessarily unexpected,” Wedbush Securities analyst Matt Bryson wrote in a note to clients. “More importantly, we believe this spate of news and speculation reiterates that in the current environment, companies with custom silicon design capabilities as well as IP blocks are in an advantageous position and that given the spate of opportunities, it's not necessarily a zero-sum game (e.g., if Marvell owns, AVGO (Google's largest TPU partner) or AMD, or NVDA are necessarily losers).” 

Marvell entered into an expanded partnership on July 29 related to Google's custom semiconductor products. “The expanded partnership spans a comprehensive range of custom silicon programs that attach to the TPU ecosystem, including AI inference accelerators, storage controllers, network interface controllers, memory interface controllers, and near-memory compute,” Marvell said in a filing.

As part of the deal, Marvell issued Google a warrant on Aug. 18 to purchase up to 58.97M shares at an exercise price of $206.58 per share.

Separately, Bryson opined this week on a potential deal between AMD (AMD) and Google (GOOG) (GOOGL) for work on a future TPU, noting such a partnership could be “significant.”

data.title: Qnity appoints semiconductor finance veteran Ken Rizvi as CFO
data.description:
• Qnity Electronics (Q) appointed semiconductor finance veteran Ken Rizvi as senior vice president and chief financial officer, effective October 1.
  • He will succeed Michael Goss, who has served as interim CFO. While, Goss will become Qnity’s vice president of finance and controllership.
  • Ken brings more than 25 years of financial experience, including extensive CFO and senior finance roles across the semiconductor ecosystem. He most recently served as CFO of Synaptics (SYNA), where he oversaw global finance, corporate development, investor relations and IT.
